paragraphs: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Marion, [Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 2:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.2.5.5); Rabbah bar Marion, [Eruvin 19a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.19a.15).
Rabbi Tanchum bar Marion, [Jerusalem Talmud Maasrot 1:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maasrot.1.2.2).

notes.text: Eruvin 19a matches the printed folio יט. The supplied transcription retains ים.

[Heilprin’s Marion index](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2548&lang=en) likewise lists Yitzchak, Rabbah and Tanchum separately. [His notice on Tanchum](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3584&lang=en) gives Rabbi Yochanan as the authority Tanchum cites in Ma’asrot.

In Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 907), the Eruvin citation reads יט, with two following points. The supplied transcription gives “ים..” for the locator. Eruvin 19a gives two attributions for the teaching about the two palms. One has Rabbi Marion reporting it in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. The other has Rabbah bar Marion teaching it in the school of Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai. The cited Jerusalem Talmud passages explicitly call Yitzchak and Tanchum “Rabbi.” The notice lists these individuals separately.
